fields.content:
Introduction to Python

What is python ?
Python is a high-level, interpreted programming language.
Python is easy to learn and is used in web development,
data science, artificial intelligence and automation.

Example:
print("Hello, World!")

Output:
Hello, World!
The print() function is used to display output on the screen.

fields.description: Learn about Variables and Data Types.
fields.content:
Variables and Data Types in Python

Variables are used to store data in a program.
A variable is created when we assign a value to it.

1. Variables

Example:

name = "Student"
age = 20
marks = 85.5

Here:
name stores text.
age stores an integer.
marks stores a decimal number.

2. Rules for Naming Variables

- A variable name must begin with a letter or underscore.
- It cannot begin with a number.
- It can contain letters, numbers, and underscores.
- Variable names are case-sensitive.
- Python keywords cannot be used as variable names.

Valid examples:

student_name = "Riya"
age2 = 20
_total = 100

3. Python Data Types

int - Stores whole numbers.

Example:
age = 20

float - Stores decimal numbers.

Example:
percentage = 85.5

str - Stores text.

Example:
name = "Python"

bool - Stores True or False.

Example:
is_student = True

list - Stores multiple items in a list.

Example:
subjects = ["Python", "Java", "DBMS"]

tuple - Stores multiple items that cannot be changed.

Example:
numbers = (10, 20, 30)

dict - Stores data in key-value pairs.

Example:
student = {"name": "Riya", "age": 20}

set - Stores unique values.

Example:
values = {10, 20, 30}

4. Checking Data Types

Python uses the type() function to check the data type.

Example:

name = "Student"
age = 20
marks = 85.5

print(type(name))
print(type(age))
print(type(marks))

Output:

<class 'str'>
<class 'int'>
<class 'float'>

5. Type Conversion

Type conversion changes one data type into another.

Example:

age = "20"
age = int(age)

marks = 85
marks = float(marks)

number = 100
text = str(number)

Conclusion:

Variables store values, and data types describe
the type of information stored in a variable.

fields.description: Learn about Conditional Statements.
fields.content:
Conditional statements are used to make decisions in Python.

Python supports if, elif, and else statements.

1. if Statement

The if statement executes code when a condition is true.

Example:

age = 20

if age >= 18:
    print("You are eligible to vote")

2. if-else Statement

The else statement executes when the if condition is false.

Example:

age = 16

if age >= 18:
    print("Adult")
else:
    print("Minor")

3. if-elif-else Statement

The elif statement checks another condition.

Example:

marks = 75

if marks >= 90:
    print("Grade A")
elif marks >= 60:
    print("Grade B")
else:
    print("Grade C")

Conditional statements help programs make decisions based on conditions.

fields.description: Learn the basics of Java programming, its features, and how Java programs work.
fields.content:
INTRODUCTION TO JAVA

1. What is Java?
Java is a high-level, object-oriented programming language.
It is used to develop desktop applications, web applications,
mobile applications, and enterprise software.
Java was developed by James Gosling and his team at Sun Microsystems.
It was released in 1995.

2. Features of Java
• Simple: Java has easy-to-understand syntax.
• Object-Oriented: Java uses classes and objects.
• Platform Independent: Java programs can run on different operating
  systems.
• Secure: Java provides security features.
• Robust: Java supports exception handling and memory management.
• Multithreaded: Java can execute multiple tasks at the same time.

3. Why is Java Platform Independent?
Java source code is compiled into bytecode.
This bytecode can run on any system that has a Java Virtual Machine (JVM).
This concept is known as:
Write Once, Run Anywhere (WORA).

4. Java Components
JDK - Java Development Kit
Used to develop and compile Java programs.

JRE - Java Runtime Environment
Provides the environment required to run Java applications.

JVM - Java Virtual Machine
Executes Java bytecode.

5. First Java Program
Example:
public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello, Java!");
    }
}

Output:
Hello, Java!

6. Explanation of the Program
public class Main
Defines a class named Main.

public static void main(String[] args)
This is the main method. Program execution starts here.

System.out.println()
Displays text on the screen.

7. Java File Name
If the class is public and named Main,
the file should be saved as:
Main.java

8. Java Applications
Java is used in:
• Android application development
• Banking applications
• Web applications
• Enterprise software
• Desktop applications

Conclusion:
Java is a popular, object-oriented, and platform-independent
programming language used to develop many types of applications.

Understand the basics of web technology, websites, browsers, servers, and how the web works.
fields.content:
INTRODUCTION TO WEB TECHNOLOGY

1. What is Web Technology?
Web technology refers to the tools, languages, and techniques used
to create and access websites and web applications.
It allows users to access information and services through the internet
using a web browser.

Examples:
• Websites
• Online shopping applications
• Online banking
• Educational websites

2. What is the World Wide Web (WWW)?
The World Wide Web is a collection of web pages and resources
connected through the internet.
Users can access these resources using a web browser.

Example:
www.google.com

3. What is the Internet?
The Internet is a worldwide network of connected computers and devices
that communicate and share information.
The WWW is a service that works over the Internet.

4. Website and Webpage
Webpage:
A single document displayed in a web browser.

Example:
A Contact Us page.
Website:
A collection of related webpages under one domain name.

Example:
A college website containing Home, About, Courses, and Contact pages.

5. Types of Websites

A. Static Website
A static website displays fixed content.
Its pages are usually created using HTML and CSS.

Example:
A simple portfolio website.

B. Dynamic Website
A dynamic website displays content that can change according to
user actions, database information, or other conditions.

Example:
Online shopping or student management website.

6. Client and Server
Client:
A device or application that requests information.
A web browser is commonly used as a client.

Server:
A computer or software that receives requests and provides
web pages or data.

Example:
Browser → Request → Web Server
Browser ← Response ← Web Server

7. Web Browser
A web browser is software used to access and display websites.

Examples:
• Google Chrome
• Mozilla Firefox
• Microsoft Edge
• Safari

8. Web Server
A web server stores, processes, and delivers website files
or responses to clients.

Examples:
• Apache
• Nginx
• Microsoft IIS

9. Frontend and Backend
Frontend:
The part of a website that users see and interact with.
Technologies:
HTML, CSS, JavaScript

Backend:
The server-side part that handles logic, data, and requests.

Technologies:
Python, Java, PHP, Django, Flask

10. Basic Web Technologies
HTML:
Used to create the structure of a webpage.

CSS:
Used to style and design webpages.

JavaScript:
Used to add interactivity and dynamic behavior.

Database:
Used to store and manage website data.

11. How a Website Works
Step 1: The user enters a website address in the browser.
Step 2: The browser finds the server using the domain name.
Step 3: The browser sends a request to the server.
Step 4: The server processes the request.
Step 5: The server sends a response to the browser.
Step 6: The browser displays the webpage.

12. URL

URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator.
It is the address used to access a resource on the web.

Example:
https://www.example.com/about
https = protocol
www.example.com = domain name
/about = path

Conclusion:
Web technology helps us create and access websites and web
applications. HTML, CSS, JavaScript, servers, and databases
work together to provide interactive web experiences.

fields.description: Learn the basic structure of HTML and create your first webpage.
fields.content:
HTML BASICS 1. What is HTML? HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It is the standard markup language used to create the structure of webpages. HTML uses tags to define elements such as headings, paragraphs, images, links, lists, and tables. 2. Basic Structure of an HTML Document Example: My First Webpage

Welcome to HTML

This is my first webpage.

3. Explanation of HTML Structure Defines the document as HTML5. The root element of an HTML document. Contains information about the webpage. Defines the title displayed on the browser tab. <body> Contains the visible content of the webpage. <h1> Defines the main heading. <p> Defines a paragraph. 4. HTML Tags and Elements An HTML element usually contains an opening tag, content, and a closing tag. Example: <p>Hello World</p> <p> is the opening tag. Hello World is the content. </p> is the closing tag. Some elements are void elements and do not need a closing tag. Examples: <br> <img> <hr> 5. HTML Heading Tags HTML provides six heading levels. <h1>Heading 1</h1> <h2>Heading 2</h2> <h3>Heading 3</h3> <h4>Heading 4</h4> <h5>Heading 5</h5> <h6>Heading 6</h6> <h1> is the largest heading level. <h6> is the smallest heading level. 6. Paragraph and Line Break Paragraph: <p>This is a paragraph.</p> Line break: <p>Hello<br>World</p> The <br> tag moves the text to the next line. 7. HTML Links The <a> tag is used to create hyperlinks. Example: <a href="https://www.google.com">Visit Google</a> The href attribute specifies the destination URL. 8. HTML Images The <img> tag is used to display an image. Example: <img src="image.jpg" alt="Sample Image"> src specifies the image location. alt provides alternative text for the image. 9. HTML Lists Ordered List: <ol> <li>HTML</li> <li>CSS</li> <li>JavaScript</li> </ol> Unordered List: <ul> <li>Python</li> <li>Java</li> <li>C++</li> </ul> <li> defines a list item. 10. HTML Comments Comments are used to write notes in HTML. They are not displayed on the webpage. Example: <!-- This is an HTML comment --> Conclusion: HTML is the foundation of webpage development. It provides the structure and content of a webpage using tags, elements, and attributes.

fields.content:
JAVASCRIPT BASICS 1. What is JavaScript? JavaScript is a programming language used to make webpages interactive and dynamic. HTML creates the structure of a webpage. CSS styles the webpage. JavaScript adds functionality and interactivity. Examples: • Displaying messages • Handling button clicks • Validating forms • Changing webpage content • Creating interactive menus 2. Adding JavaScript to HTML JavaScript can be added using the 3. Displaying Output Using console.log(): console.log("Hello JavaScript"); Output in browser console: Hello JavaScript Using alert(): alert("Welcome!"); Displays a message box. Using document.write(): document.write("Hello World"); Writes content into the webpage. 4. JavaScript Variables Variables store data. JavaScript provides three ways to declare variables: var let const Example: let name = "Rahul"; let age = 20; console.log(name); console.log(age); Output: Rahul 20 let is used for values that may change. const is used for values that should not be reassigned. var is the older way of declaring variables. 5. JavaScript Data Types Common data types: String - text Number - numeric values Boolean - true or false Undefined - variable declared but not assigned Null - intentional absence of a value Example: let studentName = "Rahul"; let marks = 85; let isPassed = true; let result; let value = null; 6. JavaScript Operators Arithmetic Operators: + Addition - Subtraction * Multiplication / Division % Modulus Example: let a = 10; let b = 5; console.log(a + b); Output: 15 Comparison Operators: == Equal value === Equal value and type != Not equal > Greater than < Less than >= Greater than or equal to <= Less than or equal to Logical Operators: && AND || OR ! NOT 7. JavaScript Conditions Example: let age = 20; if (age >= 18) { console.log("Adult"); } else { console.log("Minor"); } Output: Adult 8. JavaScript Loops for loop: for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { console.log(i); } Output: 1 2 3 4 5 while loop: let i = 1; while (i <= 3) { console.log(i); i++; } 9. JavaScript Functions A function is a block of code that performs a specific task. Example: function greet() { console.log("Hello Student!"); } greet(); Output: Hello Student! 10. JavaScript Events An event occurs when a user interacts with a webpage. Examples: • Click • Mouse movement • Keyboard input • Form submission Example: When the button is clicked, the message appears. 11. Changing HTML Content JavaScript can change webpage content using the DOM. Example:

Old Text

Explanation: getElementById() selects an HTML element by its ID. innerHTML changes the content inside that element. 12. Conclusion JavaScript is an important web development language. It works with HTML and CSS to create interactive and dynamic webpages. It is commonly used for events, form validation, animations, and changing webpage content.

fields.description: Learn how to use conditional statements to make decisions in Python.
fields.content:
Python Conditional Statements
Conditional statements are used to make decisions in a program.
They execute different blocks of code depending on whether a
condition is True or False.

Python conditional statements include:
1. if statement
2. if-else statement
3. if-elif-else statement
4. Nested if statement
5. Short-hand if statement
6. Short-hand if-else statement (conditional expression)

1. if Statement
The if statement executes a block of code when the condition
is True.

Syntax:
if condition:
    statement

Example:
age = 20
if age >= 18:
    print("You are eligible to vote.")

Output:
You are eligible to vote.

Explanation:
The condition age >= 18 is True, so the statement is executed.

2. if-else Statement
The if-else statement executes one block if the condition is
True and another block if it is False.

Syntax:
if condition:
    statements
else:
    statements

Example:
age = 16
if age >= 18:
    print("Eligible to vote")
else:
    print("Not eligible to vote")

Output:
Not eligible to vote

Explanation:
The condition is False, so the else block executes.

3. if-elif-else Statement
The elif statement means "else if".
It is used to check multiple conditions.

Syntax:
if condition1:
    statements
elif condition2:
    statements
elif condition3:
    statements
else:
    statements

Example:
marks = 75
if marks >= 90:
    print("Grade A")
elif marks >= 75:
    print("Grade B")
elif marks >= 50:
    print("Grade C")
else:
    print("Fail")

Output:
Grade B

Explanation:
Python checks conditions from top to bottom.
When a condition is True, its block executes and the remaining
conditions are skipped.

4. Nested if Statement
A nested if statement means an if statement inside another
if statement.

Example:
age = 20
has_id = True
if age >= 18:
    if has_id:
        print("Entry allowed")
    else:
        print("ID required")
else:
    print("Entry not allowed")

Output:
Entry allowed

Explanation:
The inner if statement is checked only when the outer
condition is True.

5. Short-hand if Statement
A short-hand if statement is used when only one statement
needs to execute.

Example:
age = 20
if age >= 18: print("Adult")

Output:
Adult

6. Short-hand if-else Statement
A conditional expression is used to write if-else in one line.

Syntax:
value_if_true if condition else value_if_false

Example:
age = 16
result = "Adult" if age >= 18 else "Minor"
print(result)

Output:
Minor

Explanation:
If the condition is True, "Adult" is assigned.
Otherwise, "Minor" is assigned.

7. Comparison Operators in Conditions

Comparison operators compare two values.
==  Equal to
!=  Not equal to
>   Greater than
<   Less than
>=  Greater than or equal to
<=  Less than or equal to

Example:
a = 10
b = 5
if a > b:
    print("a is greater than b")

Output:
a is greater than b

8. Logical Operators in Conditions
Logical operators combine conditions.

and:
Returns True when both conditions are True.

or:
Returns True when at least one condition is True.

not:
Reverses the result of a condition.

Example:
age = 20
marks = 80
if age >= 18 and marks >= 50:
    print("Eligible")

Output:
Eligible

Conclusion
Conditional statements help a program make decisions.
They are commonly used in grading systems, login validation,
eligibility checking and other decision-making programs.
